newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Irish President Robinson to step down Sept 12.
newsitem.headline: Irish President Robinson to step down Sept 12.

text.p: Ireland's President Mary Robinson announced on Thursday she would step down as head of state September 12, nearly three months before the official end of her term, to take up her new post as the top U.N. human rights official.
"I will retire from the presidency of Ireland on September 12 September at 1 p.m.," she told reporters, with Secretary-General Kofi Annan standing beside her.
Robinson was approved by the U.N. General Assembly on June 17 as the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights. But the date for the start of her four-year term in the Geneva-based post was left open.
Annan has been anxious for her to take over in time for the annual General Assembly session opening on September 16.
Robinson's seven-year term as president would normally end on December 2.

In making her announcement, she stumbled over the date, first saying she had indicated to Annan she would retire as president on December 12. The secretary-general then whispered in her ear and she corrected the date to September 12.
